label: D2 after a2 -> S2 (common), previous trial rewarded, late in the episode (trial >= 70)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never D1/GO) and only when the shown state is S2; 99% of mass is on a2 -> S2 common transitions (rare a1 -> S2 contributes 0.6%). It has a strong episode-time gate: silent before trial ~60, the rate rises steeply over trials 70-99 (61% of mass in trials 90-99), and it coincides with low model value. Firing also mostly needs the previous trial to have been rewarded (92% of mass); activations get larger over runs of rewarded a2/S2 trials. All variables are observed at D2 (action, state, prev_reward, ep_trial via elapsed time), so no future variables are used. Without the reward condition, D2 & a2 & S2 & ep_trial >= 70 gives F1 0.79 and mass recall 0.99. Without the time gate, precision is only 0.22. It does not fire on S1 at D2, on any D1/GO step, or early in the episode.

issues: Reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.911, R 0.814, F1 0.860, mass recall 0.903 (dev F1 0.871).

The factual claims check out against the profile. Firing is 100% at D2 and never at D1/GO. All of it is on in_state=S2, 99.4% of mass is on a2, and 99.4% is on common transitions. Activity starts at trial 50 (21 active steps in trials 50-59), and 61% of mass falls in trials 90-99. 92.5% of mass has prev_reward=1, and firing concentrates in the lowest value bins. The 'silent before ~60' wording is slightly loose (about 21 active steps in trials 50-59), but this is negligible.

Ablations agree with the explanation. Dropping the reward condition gives dev F1 0.788 and mass recall 0.991. Dropping the action condition (D2 & S2 only) drops precision to 0.71. Moving the time gate to >=65 lowers F1 to 0.83. Trials 60-69 hold only 0.3% of mass.

Small residual classes, none of them dominant: (1) a2->S2 common, trial>=70, previous trial unrewarded: precision 0.24, 7.5% of mass, usually weak activations when the trial before that also reached S2; (2) prev_reward=1 but the previous trial reached S1: precision 0.55, 3202 predicted steps, a modest false-positive pocket. Neither changes the main picture.
Alternative 'prev_reward==1 OR previous state S2' gives test F1 0.865 (vs 0.860), mass recall 0.975, precision 0.82. That is a different precision/recall trade-off, not a fix for a systematic gap.
The predicate uses no future variables, which is correct: action, state, common, prev_reward and ep_trial are all observed by D2.
